findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The revised proposal fixes the root cause in the supplied lint.ts: per-file golangci-lint runs from the project-root cwd with a cached projectDir and with --fix. It replaces them with a package-scoped run from the edited file's directory, with no --fix. It keeps config semantics by freezing the base B before the cwd changes. It also fixes the post-tool-lint wrapper, which drops warnings whenever errors also exist. The proposal doesn't overclaim: it says findings may predate the edit, gives no Cursor display claim and no guaranteed-cleanup claim, and does not report success on loader, formatter or helper failure. Its proof matrix discriminates: it includes negative controls for exclusions and checks the actual subprocess cwd and argv on both v2.0.0 and v2.13.2. I found no error that requires a change. Five non-blocking warnings: a gomod/gitroot base contract that is left undefined ('when meaningful'), temp files written outside the project root, a wrong missing-config warning when a customer config is found instead, how heavy the design is, and two collaborators (runPackagedHook, safewordCli) that this packet doesn't show.

The gomod/gitroot base is left partly open. The proposal says to keep the native result 'when meaningful' but never defines 'meaningful'. Example: a monorepo with no go.mod at the project root. There, `go env GOMOD` run from originalCwd returns /dev/null, and upstream's filepath.Dir turns that into a base of /dev. That leaves two reasonable implementations: (a) freeze B=/dev, fail to create the temp config, warn, and never lint any Go edit; or (b) treat the result as a failed lookup and warn. Both end up skipping lint, which is a regression for gomod-mode configs. Separately, freezing the outer module's or repository's base for a nested module differs from how customers usually run gomod or gitroot from inside that module (e.g. in CI). Those exclusions will then not match, and findings the customer excluded will show up again. This is noise, not a false clean result, so it is not blocking. Define 'meaningful' explicitly (e.g. GOMOD empty or os.DevNull means a failed lookup) and add a fixture for a root with no go.mod.

The temp config is written directly into B, and B can be outside the project root: an outer repository's gitroot, an outer module, or $HOME when a home config is selected in cfg mode. The proposal refuses to run any command for edited files outside the root, yet it will create and possibly leave behind (after SIGKILL) .safeword-go-lint-*.json files in directories outside the root. The residue risk is acknowledged, but this boundary asymmetry is not. Either state it explicitly or warn before writing outside projectRoot.

The existing missing-Safeword-config warning says 'linting with golangci-lint defaults, not Safeword rules'. Under the new fallback order (originalCwd, then the file's ancestors, then home), a customer config can be selected even when .safeword/.golangci.yml is missing. The warning text would then be false. Reword it for the case where a customer config was found, or emit it only on the --no-config path, as the proposal's sentence partly suggests.

This is a heavy design for a lint-hook fix: a new CLI action, YAML AST handling, placeholder rewriting for specific linters, signal handlers, and a two-version CI matrix. The proposal justifies each part with an observed regression, and that justification holds. But the set of location-sensitive keys is hand-picked (depguard, gocritic, goheader, output paths, custom plugins). Add an explicit test or inventory check against upstream placeholder and file-resource sites, so that the claim 'keep every rule/key' doesn't quietly fall behind later upstream versions.

Two collaborators can't be checked from the supplied context: Codex's runPackagedHook entry and the safewordCli resolver. The proposal requires boundary tests for both, and that is the right mitigation. The --path-prefix B approach depends on v2's base-relative issue paths; the planned tests on both v2.0.0 and v2.13.2 must confirm that real absolute paths come out when B differs from the package directory.
